source.title: Shape of U: The Nonmonotonic Relationship Between Object-Location Memory and Expectedness.

confidence_rationale: Preregistered, four-experiment, Bayes-factor-quantified human study with a clean theoretical target (the SLIMM schema model). It is the single most decisive entry for the operationalisation verdict because it shows the encoding strength of an event is NON-monotonic in expectedness: memory is best for both highly expected (schema-congruent) AND highly unexpected (high prediction-error) items, and worst for neutral ones. This directly contradicts a monotonic '1 - similarity' novelty gate, which captures only the unexpected arm. Marked 'mixed' for MECH-189: it weakens the self-contained novelty proxy as currently formulated while supporting a prediction-error-magnitude / signed-PE formulation of gate (b).
failure_signatures: A monotonic novelty gate (complexity = 1 - max cosine to anchors; higher novelty -> more write) systematically fails to write schema-congruent high-value contacts, which the U-shape shows are encoded as well as the most surprising ones.

Operationalising 'contextual complexity' as raw dissimilarity confounds two distinct encoding regimes (congruent assimilation vs incongruent encoding) that the brain routes differently; the gate cannot distinguish 'neutral/moderate' (poorly encoded) from 'strongly congruent' (well encoded).

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across four preregistered virtual-reality experiments (137 adults), object-location memory was a U-shaped function of how congruent the location was with a kitchen schema: memory was better for highly expected and highly unexpected locations than for neutral ones, consistent with the SLIMM model's prediction that both schema assimilation and prediction-error-driven encoding strengthen memory.
mapping.ree_translation: The 'high contextual complexity' term in MECH-189's WRITE gate should not be a monotonic novelty/dissimilarity measure. The biology favours an encoding signal driven by prediction-error MAGNITUDE (or a signed-PE term that admits both a schema-congruent and a schema-incongruent write regime), not 1 - similarity-to-anchors. An external PE signal naturally produces the unexpected-arm sensitivity; the congruent arm corresponds to MECH-189's adult-routine-stability intuition only if reformulated.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is object-LOCATION episodic memory in a spatial-schema task, not a cross-episode super-ordinal GOAL/value write. The U-shape is demonstrated for declarative item memory; whether value/goal anchors show the same nonmonotonicity is an inference, not a measured result. Transfer from a kitchen-schema VR task to z_world/z_goal anchors carries real risk.
mapping.source_context: Human adults, immersive VR object-location memory, preregistered, Bayes-factor inference across 4 experiments.

confidence_components.notes: Excellent methodology (preregistered, BF-quantified, replicated across 4 experiments). Mapping fidelity moderate: the nonmonotonicity result is highly relevant to the GATE SHAPE but is measured on declarative location memory, not on a goal/value write. Transfer risk elevated because the super-ordinal goal store is a different memory system from spatial-schema episodic memory.
